## Bottom line
**Suggests InSitu (73%)** · Unreliable input · Defer to expert
The input is flagged unreliable, the second model disagrees, and Invasive is in the 90% set.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | InSitu 73%, Invasive 26% | Invasive clearly plausible |
| Conformal set | InSitu, Invasive (90%) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.73 / 94th percentile, flagged | Input suspect |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Models disagree |
| Similar cases | 1 of 5 InSitu | Four neighbors Invasive |

## Tissue evidence
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (regions 3, 10) · ↑ invasive · Above typical; concept model links it to invasion [F2] · Validated
- **Marked nuclear pleomorphism** (regions 0, 2, 4) · ↑ invasive · Above typical across three regions · Validated
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 5, 6, 9) · ↓ invasive · Above typical; points away from invasion · Validated
- **Atypical cells confined within ducts** (region 11) · ↑ invasive · Below-typical score; concept model term still positive; weak spot check [F4] · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion difference 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0, so unproven. Mitoses (0/20) and necrosis (3/20) are Unreliable and score high here.

## Could be wrong if
- Simulated JPEG degradation and 94th-percentile OOD distort the region scores.
- The MUSK disagreement and four Invasive neighbors mean InSitu as top class is wrong.

## Check on the slide
1. **3, 10** — Confirm stromal infiltration versus an in situ growth pattern.
2. **11** — Check whether atypical cells are truly duct-confined.
3. **4, 5, 11** — Highest heatmap contribution; confirm what drives it.
